location_rule: This file is a DRAFT and deliberately lives under docs/hallmap/drafts/, NOT under hallthruster_bridge/prereg/. Nothing in it is decided. It becomes a pre-registration only when the owner decides every item marked PROPOSED, writes the frozen version to hallthruster_bridge/prereg/ with its own id (no '_DRAFT'), and hash-locks it, all BEFORE any design Hall map or any refined run is generated. The provenance schema (schemas/hallmap/hallmap_provenance_v1.json) refuses a convergence prereg path containing 'DRAFT'.
purpose: Numerical-convergence check for frozen DESIGN Hall maps (one map set per admitted transport member, docs/hallmap/HALLMAP_PRODUCTION_SPEC.md section 11). It asks one question: does the map content change materially when the grid, timestep or simulated time is refined? It is not a validation, does not touch the P5-N2 campaign or its fixed numerics, and never retunes transport, chemistry, wall model or B(z).
blocked_until: at least one admitted member exists (credible set is EMPTY as of 2026-09-26, hallthruster_bridge/ensemble/transport_ensemble_v0.json admission_rule_status)
Vyovrinda's own geometry and B(z) are released into the repository with a source and sha256 (none exists as of 2026-09-26)
the owner freezes this draft (every PROPOSED item decided)

baseline_numerics.status: PROPOSED (baseline = the numerics under which any member would have been admitted)
baseline_numerics.source: hallthruster_bridge/prereg/p5_n2_validation_criteria_v1.json 'no_retuning' (200 cells, dt 5 ns, 2 ms, average 1-2 ms) and every case of hallthruster_bridge/cases/p5_n2.json (cells 200, dt_s 5e-9, duration_s 0.002, average_start_s 0.001)
baseline_numerics.evidence_class: assumed (numerical setting chosen by the project; not a physical quantity)

timestepping_as_run.basis: solver defaults: hallthruster_bridge/bridge_lib.jl calls SimParams(grid=EvenGrid(cells), dt, duration, verbose=false) and passes none of these, so the SimParams keyword defaults of HallThruster.jl v0.23.1 apply (src/simulation/types.jl docstrings and keyword defaults)
timestepping_as_run.source: HallThruster.jl v0.23.1 source as installed for the bridge (Project.toml version 0.23.1); read in this lane, not executed. That this installed copy is the pinned commit bfb3019fc74ceaa2c70c9d3b19236a83a44ee3b5 is enforced by bridge check_pin() at run time but was not re-verified here: verify

solver_timestep_finding.summary: With adaptive = true (the v0.23.1 default, which the bridge does not override) the step actually taken is clamp(min(min(CFL, 0.799) * dt_iz, sqrt(CFL) * dt_E, CFL * dt_u), min_dt, max_dt), and the simulation starts from 100 * eps(). SimParams.dt is used only as the uniform step of the escape hatch that engages after max_small_steps consecutive min_dt steps. A pure 'dt -> dt/2' refinement can therefore be a no-op in runs that never enter the escape hatch.
solver_timestep_finding.source: HallThruster.jl v0.23.1 src/simulation/simulation.jl (adaptive initial step 100*eps()), src/simulation/solution.jl (adaptive step clamp and uniform-step escape hatch), src/simulation/heavy_species_update.jl (cache.dt = min(chemistry_CFL*dt_iz, sqrt(CFL)*dt_E, CFL*min_dt_u), chemistry_CFL = min(CFL, 0.799)); installed copy, identity with the pinned commit: verify
solver_timestep_finding.evidence_class: inferred (from reading the solver source; not tested by a run)
solver_timestep_finding.consequence: R2 is kept exactly as requested (dt -> dt/2) and R2b (CFL -> CFL/2) is PROPOSED as the effective time-step refinement. Owner decides which (or both) is mandatory. R2b needs a producer change (the bridge does not pass CFL today); that change is outside this lane.

refinement_design.rationale: Each refinement is compared with the SAME baseline run, so a failure can be attributed to grid, time step or run length. A combined run (R4) is optional and only diagnostic.

refinements.note: Under adaptive stepping the CFL limit also shrinks the step on the finer grid; R1 therefore tests grid and implied step together.

Per solver_timestep_finding, this changes only the escape-hatch uniform step under adaptive stepping. The producer must record whether the escape hatch engaged in the baseline and refined runs (TBD: requires a producer change; the solver does not report it in the bridge record today). If it never engaged, R2 is recorded as 'not informative', not as PASS.

Halving CFL halves the chemistry and transport step limits and scales the field limit by 1/sqrt(2) (heavy_species_update.jl formula above). Requires the bridge to pass CFL (producer change, outside this lane).

averaging_window_options.A_proposed: average over 2-4 ms (keeps the baseline's 50 % transient-discard fraction; window 2 ms)
averaging_window_options.B_alternative: average over 3-4 ms (keeps the baseline's 1 ms window length, so the I_d spectrum resolution stays 1 kHz)

refinements.num_save_rationale: num_save 2000 keeps the saved-frame spacing of the baseline (2 ms / 1000 frames). chemistry_trustworthy (f_out) and the wall-flux metrics are evaluated per saved frame, so changing the frame spacing would change how they are sampled. The bridge does not pass num_save today: producer change needed (outside this lane). If it cannot be passed, R3 runs at the default 1000 and the doubled frame spacing is recorded.
refinements.stationarity_diagnostic: report the refined run's 2-3 ms and 3-4 ms averages side by side (diagnostic only, no tolerance proposed)

refinements.note: Not part of the verdict unless the owner makes it so.

rule: all 2^d corner nodes of the map's axis box (d = number of axes)
the node nearest the box centre (ties broken by the lower index on every axis)
every node that shares a grid cell with a baseline node whose converged, sustained, chemistry_trustworthy, wall_life_trustworthy or quiet class (Id_rms_rel < 0.5) differs from a neighbour's
a stride sub-grid: every k-th node along each axis, k fixed by the owner before any refined run (CPU budget)
node_selection.applies_to: every map set separately (member x chemistry config x propellant x geometry x B-field x wall setting)
node_selection.rationale: Corners and centre probe the extremes of the operating box. Nodes next to flag or regime changes are where numerics are most likely to move a boundary; they are identified from the baseline map alone, before any refined result exists, so the selection cannot be steered by convergence outcomes.

metric_definitions.relative: delta_rel = |X_refined - X_baseline| / |X_baseline|, per node, per refinement
metric_definitions.absolute: delta_abs = |X_refined - X_baseline|, per node, per refinement (used for bounded efficiencies)
metric_definitions.both runs must have produced the observa: if either run lacks the value (solver failure), the node fails that refinement

rationale: Keeps numerical error far below the 15 % I_d tolerance used for P5-N2 validation (prereg/p5_n2_validation_criteria_v1.json D3), so resolution cannot decide whether a map node looks like the admitted closure.

Prior model-derived evidence: for quiescent xenon runs (Gaussian placeholder B, default TwoZoneBohm) 400 cells and 4 ms changed I_d by < 0.2 % (docs/HISTORY.md, section 'HallThruster.jl driver runs - P5 xenon, untuned (next-work step 1, 2026-09-25)'), about 10x inside 2 %.

Breathing runs with the measured P5 field moved their time-averaged I_d by up to 21 % between 200/400 cells and 2/4 ms (docs/HISTORY.md, section 'P5 xenon rerun with measured B(z) and facility ingestion; harness fixes (2026-09-25)'). Such nodes are meant to fail: their averages are not operating points.
discharge_power_W = I_d x V_d (hall_map_schema_v1), so it inherits this tolerance and needs none of its own.
Same order as I_d: both are time-averaged integral quantities of the same solution.

At the top of the RFP thrust band (25 mN, requirement as summarised in CLAUDE.md; verify against the RFP text) 2 % is 0.5 mN, below the 5.2-5.6 mN absolute thrust tolerances pre-registered for P5-N2 N1-N3 (D3). That comparison is context only: the P5-N2 tolerances belong to a different thruster and thrust scale and do not justify this value, which remains PROPOSED.
No in-repo convergence evidence for thrust alone exists yet (the 2026-09-25 entry reports I_d only), so the owner may prefer to tie it to I_d or loosen it.

mass_eff.label: propellant (mass) utilization, HallThruster.mass_eff
rationale: A bounded fraction: an absolute tolerance avoids inflating relative errors at low-utilization nodes.
0.02 absolute matches the 2 % relative tolerance on I_d/thrust for utilization near 1.
The owner may add current_eff (ion_current_A / discharge_current_A) with the same absolute tolerance; it is report-only in this draft.

wall_ion_flux_m2s.applies_only_to: nodes that are wall_life_trustworthy in the baseline (erosion-grade nodes). Elsewhere it is report-only because it is diagnostic there (hall_map_schema_v1)
rationale: A channel-averaged Bohm flux (loss_scale * h * sum n sqrt(Z e T_e / m)) evaluated per saved frame (hall_map_schema_v1, bridge_lib.jl wall_ion_metrics). It depends on near-wall density and T_e profiles, which are more grid-sensitive than integral quantities, hence looser than I_d/thrust.
No in-repo convergence evidence for the wall fields exists yet: 5 % is a proposal, not an inherited number.

Erosion life scales with flux times an energy-dependent sputter yield. The owner should judge 5 % against the life requirement (> 15,000 h firing within a 26,000 h mission, RFP as summarised in CLAUDE.md; verify).
Paired with the flux: erosion needs both. The sheath-plus-presheath energy (Z phi_s + T_e/2) follows the near-wall T_e, so it is proposed with the same tolerance as the flux.
Sputter yields rise steeply with ion energy near threshold, so the owner may want a tighter energy tolerance than flux tolerance. Owner decides.

categorical_invariants.rule: At every checked node, converged, sustained, chemistry_trustworthy, wall_life_trustworthy and the quiet class (Id_rms_rel < 0.5, the bridge's internal diagnostic, not a validation criterion) must be identical in the baseline and every refinement. Any flip fails that node, whatever the continuous deltas are.
categorical_invariants.chemistry_detail: chemistry_trustworthy is compared together with the per-reaction record: every reaction's extrapolated activity share stays <= 1e-12 and no unresolved table is used, in both runs (f_out = 0 is not relaxed; hall_map_schema_v1 / CLAUDE.md item 5).
categorical_invariants.rationale: A trust flag or regime that depends on resolution is a numerical artefact, not physics (compare the withdrawn v1.3 Hall hysteresis, CLAUDE.md 'Superseded'). Continuous tolerances are meaningless if the node changes regime.

fields: wall_ion_flux_m2s and wall_ion_energy_eV at non-erosion-grade nodes
report_only.note: Deltas are reported for every checked node, with no tolerance. Id_f_dominant_Hz has a resolution of 1 / window length (hall_map_schema_v1), i.e. 1 kHz for the 1 ms baseline window; differences within one bin are not differences.

verdict_rule.map_set_PASS: every checked node passes every mandatory refinement (tolerances plus categorical invariants)
verdict_rule.map_set_FAIL: any checked node fails any mandatory refinement
verdict_rule.no_post_hoc: Tolerances, node selection, mandatory refinements and averaging windows are fixed before any refined run. Failing nodes are never dropped after the fact, and numerics are never mixed within one map set.
verdict_rule.provenance: the verdict and a report sha256 go into meta.provenance.numerics.convergence; a FROZEN map set requires verdict PASS (schema allOf rule)

on_failure_options_for_owner: (a) Regenerate the whole map set at refined numerics. The member was admitted at the baseline numerics, so the owner must also decide whether the admission evidence needs a consistency re-check at the refined numerics before the maps are used.
(b) Keep the baseline and mark the failing cells non-trustworthy. This needs a consumer/schema change (hall_map_schema_v1 has no numerical-convergence node flag), which is outside this lane.
(c) Shrink the axis box to exclude the failing region, using a rule fixed in advance.
owner_decisions_required: D-C1: baseline numerics = admission numerics (200 cells, 5 ns, 2 ms, average 1-2 ms)?
D-C2: which time-step refinement is mandatory: R2 (dt/2, as requested), R2b (CFL/2), or both?
D-C3: R3 averaging window A (2-4 ms) or B (3-4 ms); num_save scaled to 2000 or left at the default?
D-C4: tolerances: I_d 2 % rel, thrust 2 % rel, mass_eff 0.02 abs, wall flux 5 % rel, wall energy 5 % rel (all PROPOSED)
D-C5: node-selection stride k, and whether the flag/regime-adjacency rule is kept
D-C7: whether R4 (combined) is only diagnostic
D-C8: producer changes needed for R2b / num_save / escape-hatch reporting (bridge_lib.jl, outside this lane)
